metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully added strikethrough to the first two Finance Meetings bullet points via Format > Text > Strikethrough, then saved with Ctrl+S.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select individual text lines in LibreOffice Impress and apply multiple character formatting operations (strikethrough, italic)
metadata.explanation: Compositional task combining the original 2-item strikethrough goal with an additional italic formatting objective on the third Finance Meetings item. The getter returns per-paragraph strike/italic state from the saved pptx; metric awards 0.33 each for the two strikethrough items and 0.33 for the italic item.

scoring_breakdown.item3_italic: 0.33 - 'Tracking budgets to reflect attendance and participation.' is italic

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the saved .pptx file from disk (file-based, no postconfig needed since file state is persisted after Ctrl+S).
Getter correctly targets slide index 4 (5th slide), matching the config's 4 pyautogui 'down' presses to navigate the slide panel.
Getter extracts per-paragraph strike and italic state keyed by stripped paragraph text, which correctly maps to the expected lookup keys.

Metric correctly accesses expected as a rules dict directly (type='rule' causes framework to pass config['rules'] as expected), using expected.get('strike_targets') and expected.get('italic_target') without an extra .get('rules') wrapping.

Expected values ('Providing another perspective...', 'Advocating for student Budget Requests.', 'Tracking budgets to reflect attendance and participation.') match the Finance Meetings bullet text confirmed by trajectory evidence.
Partial credit scoring covers all three instruction requirements: two strikethrough checks (0.67/2 each) + one italic check (0.33), totaling ~1.0.
Negative-control resistance is sound: the initial pptx state has no strikethrough or italic, so an unmodified file scores 0.0.
Error handling is present: getter returns {'error': ...} on exception, metric returns 0.0 on error/non-dict result.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The getter uses 'all(r.font.strike is True for r in runs)' which requires ALL runs to have explicitly set strike=True. If any run inherits strikethrough (font.strike returns None), the check will fail even when the text visually appears struck-through. Consider also checking font.strike is not False as a fallback, though in practice Format > Text > Strikethrough sets it explicitly on all runs.

Minor: Text key lookup is exact-match; if the pptx text contains non-breaking spaces or invisible Unicode characters, the paragraph text may not match the expected string. Consider normalizing whitespace in para_text.
